claims.statement: A `TenantScope` is built only from `profile.tenants` (itself an RLS-scoped membership read), so an unknown or foreign school code yields `null` rather than a scope; queries then add `tenant_id = scope.tenantId` as selection on top of RLS, never as authorization (rules 1–2).
`scopeForCode` matches school codes case-insensitively on both sides and `scopedPath` lowercases on the way out, so a generated link and its membership match always agree.

`SCOPED_SECTIONS` is the single compile-time list of code that lives under `/t/<code>` — `ScopedSection`, the Sidebar's section-named workspace rows and `legacyRoute` all derive from it — but nothing enumerates the route directory, so a section added outside the list is reachable yet earns no legacy redirect and no nav row, and `isScopedSection` currently has no caller.

Route composition for the scope lives in `app/(dashboard)/tenant-scope.ts` rather than the module because it joins `modules/auth` identity to tenancy's profile and only `app/` may import two private `data/` layers (rule 8); `resolveRouteScope` returns a `not-a-member` state with a fallback school instead of ever falling back to all schools.

`TenantAccess` (`granted` | `none` | `unknown`) lives in tenancy's `domain/` rather than `data/` because every module's snapshot contract must fold the verdict and another module's `data/` is private, lint-enforced by per-module `import/no-restricted-paths` zones.

`withTenantAccess` replaces only an `ok` snapshot, so a `sync-failed` or `unconfigured` result is never overwritten by the tidier "no school" story and `unknown` changes nothing; `deriveTenantAccess` maps `not-found` to `none` but `sync-failed`/`unconfigured` to `unknown`.

`getProfileSnapshot` takes the Clerk user id as a parameter instead of resolving it, because the `profiles` SELECT policy admits same-tenant rows so an explicit filter is required and the resolver sits in `modules/auth/data`, which this module cannot import.
A signed-in person with no `profiles` row is reported as `not-found` rather than `sync-failed`, keeping "provisioning has not happened yet" distinct from an error.

`ASSIGNABLE_ROLES` is deliberately narrower than `UserRole`: the UI-only `owner` has no `profile_role` enum value, so offering it would build a write Postgres rejects, and `DB_TO_UI_ROLE`/`UI_TO_DB_ROLE` are total maps so a new enum variant is a compile error.
`validateUserAccessDraft` receives `allowedTenantIds` so a submitted school outside the caller's own yields a field-level "Choose a school you have access to" instead of a bare RLS denial.

The email lookup is escaped against `ILIKE` wildcards (backslash first) and then re-checked for exact normalized equality, because `assignUserAccess` changes the role of whatever row comes back and a wildcard match would grant access to the wrong person; `not-registered` stays deliberately ambiguous so another tenant's membership is not leaked.

`assignUserAccess` runs the role UPDATE before the membership INSERT, treats zero updated rows as `denied` because an RLS-blocked UPDATE is not an error, and compensates with a best-effort `restorePriorRole` on INSERT failure — a half-applied promotion to `admin` could otherwise read and set roles across the whole unassigned profile pool.

The membership INSERT always writes `is_default: false` because the membership read policy is tenant-scoped, so an empty list for someone at another school must not be read as "no memberships" and produce a second default that makes landing depend on row order.

`public.platform_admins` carries no policy or grant for `authenticated`, so it cannot be read through the anon client and cannot be self-granted from the application; the app asks `current_user_is_platform_admin()`, a `security definer` function returning only the caller's boolean.

`isPlatformAdmin()` collapses every failure to `false` for callers where a failed check should hide a link rather than render into a denial, while the route and the Server Action use the full snapshot because they must tell `sync-failed` from `denied` (rule 24).

Platform admin is a separate axis from `profile_role`: holding `admin` at a school grants nothing on `/schools/new`, and the reach is the registry only (`tenants`, `qualifications`, `tenant_qualifications`, unassigned profiles, seating a tenant's first member) — widening it to a compliance table or letting the operator seat itself needs its own ADR (rule 30).

The platform-admin seating policy carries two load-bearing predicates — the seated `profile_id` is not the caller's and the target tenant has no members yet — and because its second predicate reads `profile_tenant_memberships`, narrowing that table's platform-admin SELECT policy silently weakens the INSERT.

`create_school` is `security invoker` so RLS evaluates every statement inside it and a non-admin gets a policy violation rather than a privilege, buying atomicity for the school and its program list without moving the security boundary.

`createSchool` distinguishes `42501` as `denied`, `23505` as `duplicate-code` and everything else as `sync-failed`, and treats a null return from the `returns uuid` function as a failure rather than a success.

The school draft validator uppercases and strips the code so `akb` cannot coexist with `AKB` as two schools that read as one — a collision the unique constraint would not catch — and rejects a code outside `[A-Z0-9]{2,12}`.

Program rows are validated in the draft's own index space — blank rows skipped, an unknown id turned into "Choose a qualification from the list", a duplicate qualification caught before the `(tenant_id, qualification_id)` constraint, and zero programs rejected — because checking against the compacted command list would file messages against the wrong row and report only the first offender.

A blank COPR number stays valid because a school is routinely entered while its certificate is still being issued, and empty optional fields become `null` rather than `''` so "not recorded" has one representation.

`createSchoolAction` sequences authorization, the qualifications lookup, `validateSchoolDraft`, then `createSchool`, returning a discriminated form state rather than throwing, and `/schools/new` renders distinct signed-out, non-admin, unconfigured and sync-failed states before the form.
An empty qualifications registry makes the add-school form unsubmittable, because a school must record at least one registered program, so the page says so instead of rendering an empty select.

`/schools/new` is deliberately not gated on `resolveRouteRole`, whose `?role=` preview override would let the screen be previewed into existence, and the platform-admin sidebar row is hidden from non-operators as usability only.
